title: How Do Restrictions on High-Skilled Immigration Affect Offshoring? Evidence from the H-1B Program
eligible_reason: Single-date design: the 2004 H-1B cap reduction. The main regressor cont_treatment = lca_emp_ratio_2001 x 1(year >= 2004) is a continuous exposure (Tables 2-5, 8, 10); binary_treatment (Table 3 col 2) is a top-dependency-group x post-2004 indicator with one adoption date. Extensive-margin tables (7, 9) are cross-sectional long differences; Table 6 uses lottery-induced excess demand in 2007-2008 as a continuous regressor in long differences.
design_notes: 00_master.do: reghdfe lemp cont_treatment, a(country_id us_id year) cluster(us_id) (line 106); reghdfe lemp binary_treatment, same FE (line 112); event-study c.cont_treatment#i.year; LD*_lemp long differences on lca_emp_ratio_2001 with naics and country FE; lottery strategy with excess_demand_07and08_adj. Firm x country x year panel from confidential BEA USDIA microdata.
data_files_note: readme.txt: BEA BE-10/BE-11 confidential microdata must be requested via researchdatagov.org; package ships 'a synthetic dataset with some of the key variables'.
software_notes: Stata reghdfe; Tables logfile.log from confidential data.
